candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a minimum of three samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether composite sampling is mandatory or only required 'if possible' affects whether the minimum sample-collection monitoring obligation is satisfied or leaves applicability unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of holding-time compliance and what counts as 'first use' can determine whether toxicity monitoring was performed as required and whether resulting test evidence is adequate or must be treated as missing/invalid.

candidates.exact_span: A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether notification occurred and whether extended holding time was permitted changes whether sample-handling requirements were met and whether absent or delayed results reflect conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How 'representative' sampling is defined for intermittent discharges affects when biomonitoring is required and whether missing results during no-discharge or episodic periods reflect non-applicability versus unresolved monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: A valid test for each species must be reported during each reporting period specified in PART I of this permit unless the permittee is performing a TRE which may increase the frequency of testing and reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Cross-reference to PART I reporting periods, the per-species validity requirement, and the TRE exception jointly determine monitoring frequency, what results should exist for compliance comparison, and whether absent data reflects altered obligations or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: One set of biomonitoring data for each species is to be recorded on the DMR for each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether one DMR entry per species per period is the operative reporting unit affects which reported measurements are available for limit comparison and whether additional collected data create separate monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: For any test which fails, is considered invalid, or which is terminated early for any reason, the full report must be submitted for agency review.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of a test as failed, invalid, or early-terminated changes whether monitoring was required to be reported on the DMR versus only submitted for review, affecting missing-evidence semantics for periods without ordinary DMR results.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit the results of each valid toxicity test on the subsequent monthly DMR for that reporting period as follows below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'subsequent monthly DMR' timing rule affects which reporting period a result belongs to and whether a gap on the expected DMR reflects delayed reporting, conditional non-requirement, or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Submit retest information clearly marked as such with the following month's DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether retest data must appear on the following month's DMR affects how retest cycles satisfy per-period monitoring obligations and how missing or late retest submissions are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Only results of valid tests are to be reported on the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: What counts as a 'valid test' determines which results are eligible for DMR-based compliance comparison versus report-only or missing-evidence treatment when tests were conducted but deemed invalid.
